measurements.scope: Each case builds one ordered I64 array or set containing 0..N-1, hashes the canonical tuple (iteration, collection) with wrapping FNV-1a, and XORs the hashes. C/Rust store the same ordered keys in an array/vector and encode the same schema directly; there is no sorting in any construction. fwp-tracing and fwp-arc use type-specialized loops (FWP_TYPED_HASH=1); fwp-arc-generic uses descriptor dispatch (FWP_TYPED_HASH=0). One unprofiled RSS/warmup process precedes twelve balanced rotating/reversed wall/child-CPU samples including startup, input construction and printing; compilation and allocation profiles are separate. All use optimization level 2; C uses -ffp-contract=off. All fwp variants use the same compiler with array and collection fusion explicitly enabled. fwp counters distinguish managed storage from hash encoding-buffer requests/capacity; collection is disabled only for ownership profiles. C counts its explicit successful application malloc; Rust counts actual application allocator calls while its vector is live. These exclude allocator-internal and stdio storage; fwp managed counts can include output values. Peak RSS comes from uninstrumented programs. Ratios above one mean extra fwp time; no parity or universal speedup is assumed.
